title: APA Style, 7th edition: citations, reference list and student paper format

source.standard: Publication Manual of the American Psychological Association, 7th edition (2020)
source.machine_form: apa.csl in this folder, verbatim from citation-style-language/styles, commit 32078ede72b9224e1ed02c546668e20ee7c75585 (2026-02-14), <updated> 2026-02-07, SHA-256 1ece4fb3c295e66d04b4394e295aa58a87741ceeef1658192437eb9953c2f13e
source.note: Rules paraphrase the manual by chapter and point to the free APA Style topic page. Section numbers are left out because they were not checked against the printed manual. Where a rule and apa.csl disagree, the CSL output for the same metadata decides the reference form.

rules.text: Every in-text citation has a reference list entry with the same first author and year, and every entry is cited in the text.
rules.source: Publication Manual 7th ed. §8.4 (consistency between citations and the list; personal communications are cited but not listed)

rules.text: A work by three or more authors is cited with the first author and et al. from the first citation; a work by one or two authors names every author each time.
Two authors are joined by an ampersand inside parentheses and by the word and in running text.
A direct quotation gives the page or paragraph number; a paraphrase does not need one.
Each claim taken from a source is cited to that source and to no other; a source is cited only for what it reports.
When a preprint and its published version both exist, the published version is cited and listed, not the preprint.
rules.source: APA 7 reference guidance: cite the published version of record when one exists

rules.text: Entries are in alphabetical order letter by letter by the author element (nothing precedes something), then by year.
rules.source: Publication Manual 7th ed. §9.44: alphabetical order of entries

rules.text: Each entry has a 0.5 inch hanging indent.
A DOI is written as a https://doi.org/ link with no DOI: label; a work without a DOI gets none invented.

The author element lists up to 20 authors in source order as Surname, Initials, with an ampersand before the final author; with 21 or more, the first 19, an ellipsis and the final author, no ampersand. A group author is written in full.
rules.source: Publication Manual 7th ed. §9.8: up to 20 authors; with 21 or more, the first 19, an ellipsis, then the last author

rules.text: The year follows the author element in parentheses with a period, (2021)., and matches the source.
A periodical entry gives volume(issue) and the page range with an en dash, never a hyphen.
Italics go on the periodical name and volume and on a book or report title, never on an article or chapter title.
Article, chapter, book and report titles are in sentence case, proper nouns kept; periodical names keep title case.
A chapter in an edited book names the editors as Initials Surname (Eds.), the book title and the chapter page range (pp. x–y), then the publisher.
A preprint entry adds the description [Preprint] after the italic title and names the archive before the DOI or URL.
rules.source: APA 7 reference type Preprint, with [Preprint] after the title

rules.text: The list starts on a label reading References, bold and centered.
All text, the reference list included, is double spaced with no extra space before or after paragraphs.
One accepted font is used throughout the text: Times New Roman 12, Calibri 11, Arial 11, Georgia 11, Lucida Sans Unicode 10 or Computer Modern 10.
Body paragraphs begin with a 0.5 inch first-line indent and are left aligned.
A level 1 heading is centered, bold and in title case.
The paper has no heading named Introduction; the paper title is the opening heading of the text.
rules.source: Publication Manual 7th ed. §2.11 and §2.27: the paper title heads the first page of text; no heading Introduction

rules.text: The reference list starts on a page of its own, after the text.
rules.source: Publication Manual 7th ed. §2.12: the reference list starts on a new page after the text

rules.text: Every listed reference is cited in the text and every in-text citation has an entry, except personal communications, which are cited in the text only.
